subject: Follow-up: Data governance items from discovery call (PII, retention, support access)
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Park <samantha.park@finservices.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Data governance items from discovery call (PII, retention, support access)

Hi Samantha — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on your requirements: 

Key points we captured during the call:
- PII scope: customer IDs, transaction metadata, and full-card PANs (tokenized by your PCI stack) — you marked PANs as "sensitive - do not store" for Redwood.
- Data residency: production models must run in the EU (Frankfurt) region; no replication to US control plane for inference payloads.
- Retention: you said logs must be kept 90 days for support/forensics, but strict model input retention should be 30 days unless flagged for investigation.
- Logging/audit: need immutable audit trail for support access, plus request/response sampling options for QA.
- Support access: preferrable model is role-based, time-limited elevation (break-glass) with multi-person approval and automated notification to FinServices security.

Attachments I dropped for your convenience: PII-mapping-template.xlsx (templated fields you can fill), support-access-matrix.csv (format we use to capture requested access levels).

Proposed next steps:
1) Samantha / Alex: populate the PII-mapping-template with expected fields by EOD Tue (2026-09-01).
2) Rishi / Ben: provide a short doc that maps Redwood support roles to the access matrix and explains the break-glass workflow (target Wed 2026-09-02).
3) Schedule a 30-min security deep-dive the week of Sept 7 to walk through technical controls (I'll send options).
4) Procurement: once the security checklist is agreed, we'll prepare contract language for data residency and retention and share a DocuSign for signature.

If anything above is off, call it out and I’ll update. 

Thanks — Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Samantha Park <samantha.park@finservices.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Ruiz <alex.ruiz@finservices.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@finservices.com>
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Data governance items from discovery call (PII, retention, support access)

Hi Vivek, thanks for capturing this. A couple quick clarifications before we populate the spreadsheet: 
- Retention: we confirmed 90 days for application logs used in investigations; however, for raw inference inputs we want a default 30-day retention with an exception process to extend to 12 months on a per-incident basis (legal sign-off required).
- Residency: EU-only for all inference data; metadata (non-PII) OK to land in our metadata store in the US if needed, but we prefer EU-only where feasible.
- Break-glass: we require 2 approvers from FinServices security for any emergency elevation and an automated e-mail to the CISO alias.

We will start filling PII-mapping-template.xlsx and return it by Tue. Also, can you flag whether Redwood can provide a redacted SOC2 report and a high-level architecture diagram showing where logs are stored (we’ll share with our InfoSec team)?

Thanks — Samantha
Samantha Park
Head of Security Operations | FinServices, Inc.

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 08:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Data governance items from discovery call (PII, retention, support access)

Vivek / Ben — following up with technical confirmations we can give FinServices to unblock procurement: 

1) Data residency
- We can pin the inference workload to eu-west-1 (Frankfurt). Inference payloads are served from the pinned region and are not replicated to US inference clusters. Control plane metadata (account-level telemetry) is stored in our control plane; for this customer we can enable a private control plane option that keeps all telemetry in EU.

2) Retention
- Retention windows are configurable per-customer. Default model input retention can be set to 30 days; audit logs can be retained for 90 days. We support an exception flow to extend retention to 12 months with an approval record attached to the log entry.

3) Support access / RBAC / break-glass
- Role-based access: support engineers have scoped roles with least-privilege by default.
- Break-glass: we have an emergency elevation mechanism that issues time-limited elevated tokens (max 4 hours) that are only granted after an approver flow. Each elevation is logged with full request/response sampling (configurable rate) and immutable append-only audit records.
- Approvals can be integrated via SAML/OIDC and we can configure a two-approver requirement; we will include automated notifications to your CISO alias.

4) Logging / sampling / redaction
- We can enable automatic redaction rules for common PII (SSNs, PANs) and user-defined redaction patterns.
- For debugging, we support request/response sampling of N% and can provide hashed-only versions for certain fields.

Attachments: I’m attaching a redacted SOC2 summary (redwood-soc2-summary-redacted.pdf) and a short architecture sketch (link in related_links). 

Suggested immediate actions:
- Vivek: send a calendar invite for the security deep-dive (30 mins) on either 2026-09-08 or 2026-09-09.
- Samantha: share the filled PII mapping + any legal clause language you need for the retention exception flow.
- Procurement: flag any contract deadlines — we aim to have an initial SOW in draft by Sept 15.

Happy to jump on a call if it helps.

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Applied ML Security | Redwood Inference

Best — Vivek
